events.subtitle: Ittetsu Takemura 2DAYS — Night 1: first Takemura/Otomo collaboration, all improvised
events.factual_description: Shinjuku PIT INN presents the first night of Ittetsu Takemura 2DAYS on Friday, October 2, 2026. Doors are at 7:00 PM and the performance starts at 7:30 PM. The announced trio is Takemura on drums, Yoshihide Otomo on guitar, and Shinpei Ruike on trumpet. PIT INN's event text states that this is Takemura's first performance with Otomo and that the night will be improvised. The published admission price is ¥4,400 including one drink; reservations and sales begin September 1.

en.why_it_matters: The first meeting is the music here. PIT INN identifies this as Takemura's first performance with Otomo and an entirely improvised set, putting Takemura's attack and elasticity against Ruike's trumpet and Otomo's guitar/noise vocabulary without a repertory safety net. That untested small-room conversation is a concrete reason to make space for the date.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room if Tokyo is available on October 2. A first-meeting improvised trio at PIT INN is the kind of evening worth building around, without turning the fact that it is a first encounter into a claim that it cannot happen again.

es.why_it_matters: Aquí el acontecimiento es el primer encuentro. PIT INN identifica esta fecha como la primera vez que Takemura toca con Otomo y anuncia una noche completamente improvisada: el ataque y la elasticidad de Takemura frente a la trompeta de Ruike y el vocabulario de guitarra y ruido de Otomo, sin repertorio que funcione como red de seguridad. Esa conversación todavía no probada en un cuarto pequeño es una razón concreta para hacerle espacio.
es.trip_verdict: Si Tokio está abierto el 2 de octubre, construiría la noche alrededor de PIT INN. Un trío de primer encuentro en improvisación libre merece prioridad, sin convertir el hecho de que sea la primera vez en una afirmación de que nunca podrá repetirse.

events.subtitle: Naruyoshi Kikuchi / Takashi Sugawa / Osamu Akimoto
events.factual_description: Shinjuku PIT INN presents Naruyoshi Kikuchi Trio on Saturday, October 10, 2026, with doors at 7:00 PM and a 7:30 PM start. The announced lineup is Kikuchi on piano, Takashi Sugawa on bass, and Osamu Akimoto on drums. In PIT INN's event note, Kikuchi says the trio was formed last year and describes its approach as 'classical free jazz'; the performance is built around Kikuchi playing piano rather than his more familiar saxophone role. Published admission is ¥5,500 advance / ¥6,050 at the door, including one drink, with ticket sales beginning September 6.

en.why_it_matters: Kikuchi's instrument choice changes the center of gravity. Rather than fronting the trio on saxophone, he puts himself at the piano inside a deliberately old-school free-jazz proposition with Sugawa and Akimoto, treating the instrument's friction and his own outsider relationship to it as part of the music. That is a specific live idea, not simply another date by a major Tokyo musician.
en.trip_verdict: Worth choosing if October 10 is open while already in Tokyo, especially if the trip has room for a late-night PIT INN set. I would not reorganize a packed Kanto itinerary around this working trio alone.

es.why_it_matters: La elección de instrumento cambia el centro de gravedad. En vez de ponerse al frente con el saxofón, Kikuchi entra al piano dentro de una propuesta deliberadamente clásica de free jazz con Sugawa y Akimoto, haciendo de la fricción con el instrumento y de su propia relación de outsider parte de la música. Esa es una idea de vivo específica, no simplemente otra fecha de un músico importante de Tokio.
es.trip_verdict: Si el 10 de octubre está libre y ya estás en Tokio, vale escoger esta noche, sobre todo si el itinerario deja espacio para PIT INN. No reorganizaría un calendario cargado de Kanto únicamente alrededor de este trío.

events.factual_description: Shinjuku PIT INN presents Shun Ishiwaka 3DAYS / 6 Performances 2026 from October 23 through October 25, 2026. October 23 and 25 daytime sets open at 2:30 PM and start at 3:00 PM; night sets open at 7:30 PM and start at 8:00 PM. On October 24 the daytime set opens at 1:30 PM and starts at 2:00 PM, while the Answer to Remember Big Band night opens at 8:00 PM and starts at 8:30 PM as one 90-minute set. The six programs are MANGAPHONICS and SMTK on October 23; an Ishiwaka/Holoubek/Chris Kazuki Jones trio and Answer to Remember Big Band on October 24; and Songbook Project plus The Boys Trio 'Returns' on October 25. Ishiwaka's official event note identifies this as the tenth edition of the 3DAYS / 6 performances format and says arrangements are being prepared specifically for the October 24 big-band set to mark the tenth edition. Published prices range from ¥4,950 advance for the October 24 daytime trio to ¥8,250 door for the October 24 big-band night; ticket sales begin September 6.

en.why_it_matters: The residency works as a portrait of Ishiwaka rather than a pile of dates. Across six sets he moves between MANGAPHONICS, SMTK, a lean trio, the large-scale Answer to Remember language, Songbook, and an older piano-trio relationship; PIT INN also marks this as the tenth edition and says the big-band charts are being prepared specifically for the occasion. The thread is Ishiwaka as drummer, organizer and composer changing the size and grammar of the ensemble around him.
en.trip_verdict: If Tokyo overlaps October 23–25, actively make room for at least one of the six sets and consider pairing contrasting formats rather than trying to collect the whole residency. The big-band night has the strongest one-off context, while the multiple active projects and three-day structure keep the weekend flexible.

es.why_it_matters: La residencia funciona como retrato de Ishiwaka, no como un montón de fechas. En seis sets pasa de MANGAPHONICS y SMTK a un trío ligero, el lenguaje de gran formato de Answer to Remember, Songbook y una relación de piano trío de muchos años; PIT INN además marca ésta como la décima edición y dice que los arreglos de la big band se están preparando especialmente para la ocasión. El hilo es Ishiwaka como baterista, organizador y compositor cambiando el tamaño y la gramática del ensamble a su alrededor.
es.trip_verdict: Si Tokio coincide con el 23–25 de octubre, sí le haría espacio activamente por lo menos a uno de los seis sets y pensaría en combinar formatos contrastantes, no en coleccionar toda la residencia. La noche de big band tiene el contexto más singular; los varios proyectos activos y los tres días dejan suficiente flexibilidad.
